$comment: Column order here is the column order of master_leads.csv. required: always = every record; no = optional (leave blank when unknown, never guess). Cross-field rules are enforced in scripts/lib/validate.mjs and documented in SCHEMA.md.

fields.name: lead_id
fields.description: Stable ID, WBM-<12 hex> derived from the primary duplicate key at first insert. Never changes afterwards.

fields.name: lead_type
fields.description: PERSON (a named individual) or ORGANIZATION (an organisation / general business contact). Never 'customer'.

fields.name: first_name
fields.description: Given name as published. Not derived by splitting full_name.

fields.name: last_name
fields.description: Family name as published.

fields.name: full_name
fields.description: Full name; built from first+last when both are given.

fields.name: email
fields.description: Only an address actually published at source_url. NEVER constructed from a naming pattern.

fields.name: email_type
fields.description: PERSONAL (named individual's address) or GENERAL_BUSINESS (info@, hello@...). Required whenever email is set; inferred from the local part if omitted.

fields.name: phone
fields.description: Only if publicly published. Kept as published.

fields.name: job_title
fields.description: Role as published.

fields.name: department
fields.description: Relevant department, e.g. Events, HR, Travel, Operations.

fields.name: company
fields.description: Organisation name. Required for ORGANIZATION records.

fields.name: website
fields.description: Organisation or personal business website.

fields.name: linkedin_url
fields.description: Public LinkedIn URL if publicly available.

fields.name: other_profile_url
fields.description: Another relevant public profile.

fields.name: industry
fields.description: Industry as published.

fields.name: organization_type
fields.description: e.g. travel agency, museum, law firm, wedding planner.

fields.name: company_size
fields.description: Only if publicly stated.

fields.name: city
fields.description: City.

fields.name: state_province
fields.description: State / province / county where relevant.

fields.name: country
fields.description: Canonical country name from config/countries.json (USA, Canada, UK, Germany...). Europe and Asia are NOT lumped.

fields.name: region
fields.description: Derived from country via config/countries.json when blank.

fields.name: pipeline
fields.description: Primary pipeline / segment.

fields.name: customer_type
fields.description: Derived from pipeline when blank (B2C, B2B, Institutional, Travel Industry, Strategic Partnership, Events/Weddings, Arts & Culture, Group Travel, Cruise, Other). A classification label only; no record is a 'customer' until the CRM says so.

fields.name: campaign
fields.description: Derived label '<pipeline> | <country> | <intent class>' when blank, e.g. 'B2C Broad | USA | Broad Prospect'.

fields.name: intent_class
fields.description: Broad vs intent. Defaults to BROAD_PROSPECT. TRAVEL_INTENT / EVENT_INTENT / SEASONAL_OPPORTUNITY / DESTINATION_INTEREST need intent_evidence.

fields.name: intent_type
fields.description: What the evidence shows (e.g. Honeymoon, Christmas travel, Cruise). 'None Identified' when there is no evidence.

fields.name: travel_category
fields.description: Travel category relevant to the lead (leisure, corporate, cruise, cultural...).

fields.name: destination_interest
fields.description: A DATA FIELD, never a campaign. Only if the source explicitly shows interest in a destination.

fields.name: seasonal_opportunity
fields.description: e.g. Christmas 2026. Only with evidence; never assumed for a whole market.

fields.name: event_opportunity
fields.description: Specific event the lead relates to, only with a source.

fields.name: potential_use_case
fields.description: Potential WBM use case (e.g. corporate retreat, honeymoon design, institutional group travel).

fields.name: relevance
fields.description: Operational priority, not a probability. Never a conversion prediction.

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: URL supporting the lead (identity / organisation / email / title / intent).

fields.name: source_type
fields.description: Category of the source.

fields.name: discovery_date
fields.description: YYYY-MM-DD first discovery date.

fields.name: discovery_method
fields.description: How it was found, e.g. 'web search: UK travel advisors', 'directory listing'.

fields.name: evidence
fields.description: Short factual note on what the source shows (identity, role, where the email appears). No sensitive personal data.

fields.name: intent_evidence
fields.description: Quote/paraphrase and URL of the public statement of travel intent. Required for any intent class that is not BROAD/CORPORATE/PARTNERSHIP.

fields.name: duplicate_key
fields.description: Highest-priority dedupe key (email:... / profile:... / person:... / org:...). Unique across the master.

fields.name: existing_match
fields.description: lead_id of another record at the same organisation that was kept separate (a different contact). Not a duplicate marker.

fields.name: lead_status
fields.description: DISCOVERED, ENRICHED, READY_FOR_OUTREACH (DUPLICATE and OUT_OF_SCOPE are reported but not stored in master).

fields.name: source_history
fields.description: Every source seen for this lead, ' || ' separated: date|source_type|url. Appended on enrichment, never rewritten.

fields.name: last_updated
fields.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the last legitimate update.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Free notes. No sensitive personal information.
